data.name: Qasima
data.gender_notes: Qasima is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Qasima is an Arabic name that means 'forgiving' or 'merciful'. It is derived from the root word 'qasama' which means 'to forgive'. The name Qasima carries the meaning “Forgiving” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Qasima usually hope their child will grow to embody forgiving and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: One who is merciful and forgiving, reflecting the qualities of Allah.
data.etymology: Qasima belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Forgiving.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Qasima total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_arabic.name: قاسم
in_arabic.meaning: أصل الاسم قاسم من الجذر ق س م، يعني القاسم، الموزع، المُقسم
in_arabic.long_meaning: أصل الاسم قاسم من الجذر ق س م، يعني القاسم، الموزع، المُقسم. يُعد قاسم أحد أسماء الله الحسنى المذكورة في القرآن، ويُشير إلى فضل الله في توزيع رزقه بين عباده. يُستخدم اسم قاسم في بعض الأماكن ليعني المالك الأكبر، ويُستشهد به أيضًا في بعض الآيات القرآنية كقوله تعالى {قَسَموا أَموالَهُم فَما كَانَ عَلَى الْقَوِيِّ مِنْهُم مِن حِسَابٍ وَلَكِن ذُكِرَ الْمِسْكِينُ} [النور:32]

in_urdu.name: قاسم
in_urdu.meaning: اسم قاسم کا معانی ہے قاسم، تقسیم کرنے والا، میں کھانے والا
in_urdu.long_meaning: اسم قاسم کا اہمیت اسلام میں ہے، یہ نام الله تعالی کا نام ہے جو قرآن میں مذکور ہے،یہ نام تقسیم کرنے والا یا میں کھانے والا کے معنی میں آتا ہے، یہ نام بہت ہی اچھا نام ہے جو کسی بچے کو دینے سے ان کے مستقبل کے لیے اچھا ہوگا، اللہ تعالی نے ہم سب سے رزق تقسیم کیا ہے، اور ہم اس کی قدر کرنی چاہئے

in_hindi.name: क़ासिम
in_hindi.meaning: क़ासिम का अर्थ है किसी को में खाने वाला, बांटने वाला, प्राप्त करने वाला
in_hindi.long_meaning: क़ासिम नाम का महत्व इस्लाम में है, यह नाम अल्लाह का नाम है, जो कुरान में वर्णित है, जिसका अर्थ है साझा करने वाला या में खाने वाला, यह नाम बहुत ही अच्छा है, जिसको किसी बच्चे को देने से उनके भविष्य के लिए अच्छा होगा, अल्लाह ने हमें सब से साझा किया है, जिसकी हमें कद्र करनी चाहिए

in_pashto.meaning: قاسم د هغه کس ته ورځونکي کېږي چې د هغه د ګټو دوه نایسې برخې په درنه کې ویشي

in_english.name: Qasima
in_english.meaning: Qasima is a name that means distributor, divider, sharer, receiver, or the one who divides and distributes
in_english.long_meaning: Qasima is a name derived from the Arabic root Q-S-M, which means distributor, divider, sharer, receiver, or the one who divides and distributes. It is one of the beautiful names of Allah mentioned in the Quran, referring to the blessings of Allah in distributing His provisions among His servants. In some contexts, the name Qasima is used to mean the owner or the one who owns something, and it is also referenced in some Quranic verses such as {They have divided their capital amongst themselves, so they will not be asked about their account} [The Light:32].

data.cultural_impact: The name Qasima holds significant cultural importance in Islamic societies, as the Islamic faith emphasizes the importance of forgiveness and compassion towards others. In Muslim communities, the name is given to remind parents and the child of the importance of showing kindness, generosity, and forgiveness towards others. The name is also seen as a reminder of God's mercy and forgiveness towards His creation.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Qasima holds deep significance for Muslims. In Islam, forgiving others is considered a sacred act and a means to draw closer to God. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, ".....and he who pardons, Allah will pardon him" [Bukhari 2456]. By choosing the name Qasima, parents are instilling in their child the importance of emulating God's mercy and forgiveness towards others. It is a constant reminder of the spiritual value of forgiveness and the role it plays in cultivating a compassionate and virtuous character.
